match.reason: The bank's Rewards point only defines performance pay as one type of reward and does not teach its trade-off, that it can lift effort but push staff to compete rather than cooperate, so no existing point teaches this idea.

draft.title: Performance-related pay
card: Performance-related pay links part of an employee's pay to results. The results may be those of the employee, a team or the whole business.
a one-off payment for reaching a target, such as a set level of sales.
a payment worked out as a share of what the employee sells.
a share of the business's profit paid to staff. These payments can lift effort, because extra work leads to extra pay, but they may push staff to compete instead of cooperating.
draft.remember: Pay tied to results can lift effort, but it may also reduce teamwork.

a.q: Which of these is an example of performance-related pay?
opts: A real estate agent is paid a share of each home sold
A cleaner is paid the same wage for every hour worked
A nurse is given a free course on first aid
A clerk is given a warning for being late
a.why: The agent's pay rises with the sales made, so it is linked to results. A fixed hourly wage does not change with results. A free course is training, not pay for results.
a.clue: Which payment changes depending on what the worker achieves?

b.q: Priya manages a car yard in Geelong. She pays each salesperson a commission on their own sales only. Which problem is most likely to result?
opts: Salespeople may compete and not help each other
Salespeople may lose all reason to sell more cars
Salespeople may share leads more often than before
Salespeople may be paid even when they sell no cars
b.why: Commission on individual sales rewards each person's own results, so staff may guard customers and leads instead of cooperating. The pay still rewards extra sales, so it does not remove the reason to sell more.
b.clue: Think about who gains when a colleague makes the sale.

a.best: A real estate agent is paid a share of each home sold

b.best: Salespeople may compete and not help each other

problems.detail: The general effect ('These payments can lift effort... but they may push staff to compete') sits inside the profit share bullet. A student could read it as applying only to profit shares, not to bonuses and commissions as well. It should be its own bullet.

proposal.title: Performance-related pay
card: Performance-related pay links part of an employee's pay to results. The results may be those of the employee, a team or the whole business.
A bonus is a one-off payment for reaching a target, such as a set level of sales. A commission is a payment worked out as a share of what the employee sells.
A profit share pays staff a share of the business's profit, so it rewards the results of the whole business.
All three types can lift effort, because extra work can lead to extra pay. But they may push staff to compete instead of cooperating.
proposal.remember: Pay tied to results can lift effort, but it may also reduce teamwork.
